CIRCLELOGIC OS / V05 BACKEND PILOT

From preview to
a real connection test.

Run the backend privately, connect an approved Microsoft test mailbox, and verify one appointment.

No live Microsoft account was connected during development. The screenshots below are from the actual application using synthetic test responses. This guide is not a dashboard and does not accept credentials.
01

Start the application on your computer

Extract the full ZIP. Open circlelogic-os and double-click START-CIRCLELOGIC.cmd. Python 3.11+ and approved package-download access are needed. Keep the terminal window open and use http://localhost:8000. Do not open the old preview or frontend HTML file.

On macOS/Linux: python3 launcher.py start. The local starter does not publish the app or open a firewall port.

02

Create your private testing workspace

Run CREATE-PRIVATE-WORKSPACE.cmd. Choose your own username and private password, then sign in and enrol an authenticator. Save the recovery codes privately. The published testing123 account is only for fabricated-data checks, not for a real mailbox.

03

Check that the backend is running

Open API Connections → Check backend setup. The checks confirm the local API, database, vault and MFA. Copy the exact Microsoft callback displayed. These checks do not yet make provider requests.

04

Have Microsoft access approved

Ask the administrator to arrange an approved Microsoft 365 test mailbox and a dedicated single-tenant app registration. Use the organisation that owns that mailbox. Record the Application client ID, Directory tenant ID and a short-lived client secret Value (not Secret ID).

Add the exact CircleLogic callback as a Web redirect, not SPA. The default is http://localhost:8000/api/oauth/microsoft/callback. Request delegated Calendars.ReadBasic; the flow also requests offline_access. No email or calendar-write permissions are requested by this app.

Official Microsoft instructions: Register an application · Web redirect · Secret Value / production alternatives · Calendar permissions

05

Use the enabled credential form

Open Diary / Calendar → Add API. Enter the three values, or fill and upload the supplied blank JSON template. Uploading only fills the form. It does not save or connect until you review it and choose Save credentials.

Next select Authorise Microsoft, choose the correct test mailbox and complete consent. Saving credentials alone is not authorisation.

06

Test and sync

After Microsoft returns you to the app, open Calendar → Manage → Test and sync. The backend imports the next 30 days from that account's default calendar. Connection checks explains the saved, authorised and imported stages; its report omits tokens and appointment content.

07

Prove the data is right

Create TEST - CircleLogic inspection tomorrow in the test mailbox's default Outlook calendar. Do not invite real people. Sync, compare the title, time and location, then update and delete the event in Outlook and sync after each change. Test twice to check there are no duplicates. The dashboard displays Sydney time.

Only the calendar panel fills from this connection. CRM, market and buyer-score widgets remain empty until their own feeds exist and import successfully. An empty calendar can legitimately return zero events; sample records are never inserted into the running app.

Before customer use: real-account acceptance, native browser OAuth and HTTPS deployment testing are still required. Microsoft/REA adapters are implemented; Agentbox, Australian RP Data and Proping remain unfinished. Protect the local database and master key. Use approved hosting and private customer identities, not this testing database, for production.
